text.errorPlaceholder: e.g. Picking from the wrong location
text.testPlaceholder: e.g. Scan a test label of a wrong location: the scanner must block the pick
text.notePlaceholder: e.g. Tested with the red test label, blocked at once
text.reasonPlaceholder: e.g. Test room occupied, guest extended the stay
text.lastNote: The date it was last proven to work before it came into this register. Every check you record afterwards moves it on.
text.effectNote: Errors per month before the device and since, from your own defect or complaint log. Optional: they give the effectiveness.
text.intervalNote: Each shift and daily: due again the next day (the register counts days, not shifts; record one check per shift if you test every shift). Weekly: 7 days. Monthly: 30 days. These are defaults; choose what your risk needs.
text.verifyNote: Verify means: feed the device the error it should catch and see it react. A failed check marks the device failed until a later check says it works.
text.complianceNote: Verification compliance = due checks done on time ÷ due checks in the period. A check falls due on the last verified date plus the interval and is on time when the device was tested (works or failed) on or before that date. Each further interval that passes without a test counts as one more missed check, and a late test restarts the clock. A check due today counts only once it is done; “not tested” is not a test.
text.failureNote: Failure rate = failed tests ÷ tests (works + failed) in the period. Not tested is left out.
text.effectivenessNote: Effectiveness = (errors per month before − after) ÷ before, for devices with a before above 0. Your own figures; a few months after the device came in tell more than one.
text.strengthNote: Prevention is stronger than detection (the error cannot happen at all, instead of being caught before it leaves the step), and control is stronger than warning (the process stops, instead of a signal someone can miss). Strongest first.
text.checklistNote: Tick on paper while you test, then record the results here. Each-shift devices have one box per shift.
text.failedHandoff: The device is marked failed. Until it is repaired and a check says it works, the error it guards against is not protected: contain it with a 100 % manual check.
text.empty: No device in the register yet.

methods.name: Contact
methods.hint: Checks a physical or sensed attribute: shape, size, weight, colour, a barcode, a sensor.

methods.name: Fixed-value (constant number)
methods.hint: Checks that the right number of parts or moves is there: a count, a kit, a pre-counted set.

methods.name: Motion-step (sequence)
methods.hint: Checks that the steps happen in the right order: the next step only opens when the one before is done.

functions.name: Control: stops the process or makes the error impossible
Warning: signals the error, a person has to react

levels.name: Detection: the error is caught before it leaves the step

failed.meaning: A device that failed its test is not protecting anything: the error it was built for can happen again and leave the step unseen.
moves: Contain it now: a 100 % manual check at the step until the device works again, with a name on it.
Find why it failed (bypassed, worn, changed settings, a software update) before you only repair it.
Repair it, test it with the deliberate error again and record the result here.
failed.question: Who could have bypassed or changed it, and would we have noticed without this test?

overdue.meaning: An overdue device may still work, but nobody has proven it. A poka-yoke that is not tested is a hope, not a protection.
moves: Test the most overdue device on this shift, with the deliberate error.
Ask the owner what stopped the check: time, the test part, access to the equipment.
If the interval cannot be kept, change the interval or the owner, not the habit of skipping.
overdue.question: What would it take for this check to happen without anyone having to remember it?

new.meaning: A device that was never verified has never been proven. Register it with the date it was last tested, or test it today.
moves: Write how to test it: the deliberate error and the reaction you expect.
Test it today and record the result.
Give it an owner and an interval.
new.question: How would we know tomorrow if this device stopped working tonight?

weak.meaning: Every device works and is tested on time. The next gain is strength: devices that only detect or only warn still let the error happen.
moves: Take the detection + warning devices first: can the warning become a stop?
Ask whether the error could be made impossible earlier in the process.
Check the before and after figures: where the errors did not fall, the device is in the wrong place.
weak.question: Which of these errors could we design out so that no check is needed at all?

tips: Test it with a deliberate error.
A device is verified when someone feeds it the error it should catch (a label of a wrong location, an underweight parcel, an unscanned label) and it reacts. Looking at it is not a test.
Until a later check says it works, the error it guards against can reach the customer. Contain it with a manual check and send the repair to the Action Tracker.
Prevention beats detection, control beats warning.
A device that makes the error impossible is stronger than one that finds it; one that stops the process is stronger than a light or a beep that someone can ignore.
A check that could not be done (the test room was occupied, the line could not stop) is recorded with its reason; the device stays due.
Write the failure mode the device answers. After a few months the before and after figures show whether its rating in the FMEA may change.

devices.name: Pick-location scan check
devices.step: Picking: scan the location, then the item
devices.test: Scan the red test label of a wrong location: the scanner must refuse the pick.

devices.name: Weight check at packing
devices.error: Parcel with a missing or an extra item
devices.step: Packing: weigh before the parcel is closed
devices.test: Put the 50 g test weight on a packed order: the scale must send it to the reject lane.
notes: Test parcel passed: scale out of calibration after it was moved.
Scale recalibrated by the supplier, test weight rejected again.

devices.name: Colour-coded totes per carrier
devices.error: Tote put on the wrong outbound lane
devices.step: Sorting: tote to the lane of its colour
devices.test: Walk the lanes: every tote and lane sign in its carrier colour, no faded or missing labels.

devices.name: Label printer interlock
devices.error: Shipping label on the wrong parcel
devices.step: Packing: the label prints only after the parcel is scanned and weighed
devices.test: Try to print a label without scanning the parcel: the printer must not print.
notes: Label printed without the scan: the interlock was switched off after the printer firmware update.

devices.name: Pallet height gauge at the dock
devices.error: Pallet too high for the racking
devices.step: Inbound: every pallet passes under the gauge bar
devices.test: Measure the bar at 1.80 m and push a pallet that is too high: it must not pass.

devices.name: Key card encoder read-back
devices.error: Key card encoded for the wrong room or dates
devices.step: Check-in: the encoder reads the card back against the reservation
devices.test: Encode a card for test room 999 with yesterday's date: the encoder must show the mismatch.
devices.fmea: Key card encoded for the wrong room
untested: Encoder in use the whole shift: check-in queue of a tour group.

devices.name: Minibar sensor
devices.step: Room: the sensor posts each item taken to the room bill
devices.test: Lift one item in the test room: the charge must appear on the room within 10 minutes.
untested: Test room occupied, the guest extended the stay.

devices.name: Room-ready checklist lock in the PMS
devices.error: Room released to sale before the inspection is complete
devices.step: Housekeeping: status “inspected” only when every checklist line is ticked
devices.test: Leave one checklist line open and try to set the room to inspected: the PMS must refuse.

devices.name: Breakfast entitlement scan
devices.error: Breakfast served without a breakfast package
devices.step: Restaurant entrance: scan the room's key card
devices.test: Scan the test card of a room without breakfast: the scanner must show the red notice.
notes: Every room showed as entitled after the PMS interface restart.
Interface mapping restored by IT, test card shows the notice again.

devices.name: Pre-counted amenity kit
devices.error: Room set up with an amenity missing
devices.step: Housekeeping: one sealed kit per room, counted in the store
devices.test: Open five kits at random and count them against the kit card.
